text: The $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Theory}$ states that:
explanation: One of the fundamental principles of the $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Theory}$ is that all known $\text{Living}$ $\text{Things}$ are $\text{Composed}$ of $\text{One}$ or $\text{More}$ $\text{Cells}$. Another key tenet is that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

text: The $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Vessel}$ that $\text{Carries}$ $\text{Deoxygenated}$ $\text{Blood}$ from the $\text{Heart}$ to the $\text{Lungs}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the heart and pulmonary circulation]
explanation: The $\text{Pulmonary}$ $\text{Artery}$ is unique because it is an $\text{Artery}$ that $\text{Carries}$ $\text{Deoxygenated}$ $\text{Blood}$ (from the $\text{Right}$ $\text{Ventricle}$) to the $\text{Lungs}$ for $\text{Oxygenation}$.

text: The $\text{Organelle}$ responsible for $\text{Protein}$ $\text{Synthesis}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a Ribosome translating mRNA]
explanation: $\text{Ribosomes}$ are the $\text{Cell's}$ $\text{Protein}$ $\text{Factories}$. They $\text{Read}$ the $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Code}$ on $\text{mRNA}$ and $\text{Assemble}$ $\text{Amino}$ $\text{Acids}$ into $\text{Polypeptide}$ $\text{Chains}$ ($	ext{Proteins}$).

text: Which of the following conditions is necessary for $\text{Photosynthesis}$ to $\text{Occur}$?
image: [Diagram of a chloroplast and the overall process of Photosynthesis]
explanation: $\text{Photosynthesis}$ is the process by which $\text{Plants}$ use $\text{Sunlight}$ $\text{Energy}$ to $\text{Convert}$ $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ and $\text{Water}$ into $\text{Glucose}$ and $\text{Oxygen}$.

text: The $\text{Deficiency}$ of $\text{Vitamin}$ $\text{C}$ in $\text{Humans}$ causes:
explanation: $\text{Scurvy}$ is caused by a $\text{Lack}$ of $\text{Ascorbic}$ $\text{Acid}$ ($	ext{Vitamin}$ $\text{C}$), which is necessary for $\text{Collagen}$ $\text{Production}$ and tissue repair.

text: A $\text{Flower}$ that $\text{Possesses}$ both the $\text{Stamen}$ and the $\text{Pistil}$ is described as:
image: [Diagram of a bisexual (hermaphroditic) flower]
explanation: A $\text{Bisexual}$ $\text{Flower}$ (or $\text{Hermaphroditic}$ $\text{Flower}$) contains both $\text{Male}$ $\text{Reproductive}$ $\text{Organs}$ ($	ext{Stamen}$) and $\text{Female}$ $\text{Reproductive}$ $\text{Organs}$ ($	ext{Pistil}$ or $\text{Carpel}$) in the same structure.

text: The $\text{Organ}$ in the $\text{Human}$ $\text{Body}$ that $\text{Produces}$ $\text{Bile}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the human liver and gall bladder]
explanation: The $\text{Liver}$ is the $\text{Largest}$ $\text{Internal}$ $\text{Organ}$ and is responsible for the $\text{Production}$ of $\text{Bile}$. The $\text{Gall}$ $\text{Bladder}$ only $\text{Stores}$ and $\text{Concentrates}$ the $\text{Bile}$.

text: Which of the following $\text{Excretory}$ $\text{Products}$ is $\text{Stored}$ in the $\text{Bladder}$ of $\text{Mammals}$?
image: [Diagram of the human urinary system]
explanation: The $\text{Urinary}$ $\text{Bladder}$ is a $\text{Muscular}$ $\text{Sac}$ that $\text{Stores}$ $\text{Urine}$ (a solution of $\text{Water}$, $\text{Urea}$, and $\text{Salts}$) before it is eliminated from the body.

text: The $\text{Waste}$ $\text{Product}$ of $\text{Photosynthesis}$ that is $\text{Released}$ into the $\text{Atmosphere}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Oxygen}$ $\text{Gas}$ is produced as a $\text{By}$-$\text{Product}$ when $\text{Water}$ is $\text{Split}$ during the $\text{Light}$-$\text{Dependent}$ $\text{Reactions}$ of $\text{Photosynthesis}$.

text: Which of these is $\text{NOT}$ a $\text{Function}$ of the $\text{Skin}$?
explanation: While the skin can synthesize $\text{Vitamin}$ $\text{D}$ (a $\text{Steroid}$ $\text{Hormone}$) under $\text{UV}$ $\text{Light}$, it is $\text{Not}$ considered a $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Endocrine}$ $\text{Gland}$ that $\text{Secretes}$ $\text{Hormones}$ like the $\text{Thyroid}$ or $\text{Pituitary}$.

text: A $\text{Population}$ refers to the $\text{Total}$ $\text{Number}$ of:
image: [Image illustrating a population of a single species in a defined area]
explanation: In $\text{Ecology}$, a $\text{Population}$ is defined as a group of individuals belonging to the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Species}$ that $\text{Live}$ in the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Geographical}$ $\text{Area}$ and are $\text{Capable}$ of $\text{Interbreeding}$.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Plant}$ where $\text{Fertilization}$ $\text{Occurs}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a flower showing the ovules inside the ovary]
explanation: The $\text{Ovary}$ contains the $\text{Ovules}$, which house the $\text{Egg}$ $\text{Cell}$. The $\text{Male}$ $\text{Gamete}$ ($	ext{Pollen}$ $\text{Tube}$) $\text{Fuses}$ with the $\text{Egg}$ $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Inside}$ the $\text{Ovule}$ within the $\text{Ovary}$.

text: Which of the following $\text{Classes}$ of $\text{Food}$ is $\text{Primarily}$ $\text{Used}$ for $\text{Growth}$ and $\text{Repair}$?
image: [Image showing sources of protein]
explanation: $\text{Proteins}$ are $\text{Building}$ $\text{Blocks}$ of the $\text{Body}$. They are $\text{Essential}$ for the $\text{Formation}$ of $\text{New}$ $\text{Cells}$ and $\text{Tissues}$ ($	ext{Growth}$) and $\text{Replacing}$ $\text{Worn}$-$\text{Out}$ $\text{Parts}$ ($	ext{Repair}$).

text: The $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Material}$ in a $\text{Bacteria}$ is $\text{Located}$ in the:
image: [Diagram of a prokaryotic cell showing the nucleoid region]
explanation: $\text{Bacteria}$ are $\text{Prokaryotic}$ cells, meaning they $\text{Lack}$ a $\text{True}$ $\text{Membrane}$-$\text{Bound}$ $\text{Nucleus}$. Their $\text{Single}$ $\text{Circular}$ $\text{Chromosome}$ is $\text{Located}$ in an $\text{Irregular}$ $\text{Area}$ of the $\text{Cytoplasm}$ called the $\text{Nucleoid}$ $\text{Region}$.

text: The $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Gases}$ between the $\text{Blood}$ and $\text{Body}$ $\text{Tissues}$ occurs through the $\text{Process}$ of:
image: [Diagram illustrating gas exchange (O2 and CO2) across a capillary wall]
explanation: The $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Oxygen}$ and $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ across the $\text{Capillary}$ $\text{Walls}$ and into or out of the $\text{Tissue}$ $\text{Cells}$ is a form of $\text{Simple}$ $\text{Diffusion}$, moving from a $\text{High}$ $\text{Concentration}$ to a $\text{Low}$ $\text{Concentration}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Receptors}$ is $\text{Responsible}$ for $\text{Sense}$ of $\text{Touch}$ and $\text{Pressure}$?
image: [Diagram showing various sensory receptors in the skin layers]
explanation: $\text{Mechanoreceptors}$ are $\text{Sensory}$ $\text{Receptors}$ that $\text{Respond}$ to $\text{Mechanical}$ $\text{Forces}$ such as $\text{Touch}$, $\text{Pressure}$, $\text{Vibration}$, and $\text{Stretch}$.

text: The $\text{Habitat}$ of a $\text{Tapeworm}$ is best described as:
explanation: A $\text{Tapeworm}$ ($	ext{Taenia}$) $\text{Lives}$ $\text{Inside}$ the $\text{Intestine}$ of a $\text{Host}$ (like a human or animal), $\text{Feeding}$ on $\text{Digested}$ $\text{Food}$ and $\text{Causing}$ $\text{Harm}$, which defines it as a $\text{Parasitic}$ $\text{Habitat}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Maintaining}$ a $\text{Constant}$ $\text{Internal}$ $\text{Environment}$ in an $\text{Organism}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Homeostasis}$ is the $\text{Ability}$ of the $\text{Body}$ to $\text{Maintain}$ a $\text{Stable}$ $\text{Internal}$ $\text{Environment}$ despite $\text{Changes}$ in the $\text{External}$ $\text{Environment}$ (e.g., $\text{Temperature}$, $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Sugar}$ $\text{Levels}$).

text: Which of the following $\text{Nutrients}$ provides the $\text{Highest}$ $\text{Amount}$ of $\text{Energy}$ per $\text{Gram}$?
image: [Bar chart comparing energy yield of Fats, Proteins, and Carbohydrates]
explanation: $\text{Fats}$ $\text{Provide}$ approximately $\text{9}$ $\text{Kcal}$ per $\text{Gram}$, while $\text{Carbohydrates}$ and $\text{Proteins}$ provide about $\text{4}$ $\text{Kcal}$ per $\text{Gram}$. They are the most $\text{Concentrated}$ $\text{Energy}$ $\text{Source}$.

text: The $\text{Region}$ of $\text{Rapid}$ $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Division}$ in a $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Root}$ $\text{Tip}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a root tip highlighting the region of cell division]
explanation: The $\text{Apical}$ $\text{Meristem}$ at the $\text{Tip}$ of the $\text{Root}$ is the $\text{Zone}$ of $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Division}$, where cells $\text{Undergo}$ $\text{Mitosis}$ to $\text{Produce}$ $\text{New}$ $\text{Cells}$ for $\text{Growth}$.

text: The $\text{Inheritance}$ of $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Groups}$ in $\text{Humans}$ is an example of:
image: [Punnett square illustrating ABO blood group inheritance]
explanation: The $\text{ABO}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Group}$ system involves $\text{Three}$ $\text{Alleles}$ ($	ext{Multiple}$ $\text{Alleles}$: $\text{I}^{\text{A}}$, $\text{I}^{\text{B}}$, $\text{i}$), and the $\text{Alleles}$ $\text{I}^{\text{A}}$ and $\text{I}^{\text{B}}$ are $\text{Equally}$ $\text{Expressed}$ in the $\text{AB}$ blood type ($	ext{Co}$-$\text{dominance}$).

text: Which of these $\text{Organisms}$ belongs to the $\text{Phylum}$ $\text{Mollusca}$?
explanation: The $\text{Phylum}$ $\text{Mollusca}$ includes $\text{Snails}$, $\text{Slugs}$, $\text{Octopuses}$, $\text{Squids}$, and $\text{Clams}$. They are characterized by a $\text{Soft}$ $\text{Body}$, often $\text{Protected}$ by a $\text{Shell}$.

text: The $\text{Function}$ of the $\text{Placenta}$ in $\text{Mammals}$ is to:
image: [Diagram showing the placenta connecting the mother and fetus]
explanation: The $\text{Placenta}$ is a $\text{Temporary}$ $\text{Organ}$ that $\text{Connects}$ the $\text{Developing}$ $\text{Fetus}$ to the $\text{Uterine}$ $\text{Wall}$ and $\text{Facilitates}$ the $\text{Transfer}$ of $\text{Oxygen}$, $\text{Nutrients}$, and the $\text{Removal}$ of $\text{Fetal}$ $\text{Wastes}$.

text: In $\text{Monocot}$ $\text{Plants}$, the $\text{Vascular}$ $\text{Bundles}$ are $\text{Scattered}$ in the $\text{Stem}$, while in $\text{Dicot}$ $\text{Plants}$ they are $\text{Arranged}$ in a:
image: [Cross-sections comparing Monocot and Dicot stems]
explanation: A $\text{Key}$ $\text{Difference}$ between $\text{Monocots}$ and $\text{Dicots}$ is the $\text{Arrangement}$ of $\text{Vascular}$ $\text{Bundles}$ in the $\text{Stem}$. $\text{Dicots}$ have a $\text{Neatly}$ $\text{Arranged}$ $\text{Ring}$ of $\text{Vascular}$ $\text{Bundles}$.

text: The $\text{Hormone}$ that $\text{Lowers}$ the $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Glucose}$ $\text{Level}$ in $\text{Humans}$ is:
image: [Diagram illustrating the roles of Insulin and Glucagon in blood sugar regulation]
explanation: $\text{Insulin}$, secreted by the $\text{Pancreas}$, $\text{Promotes}$ the $\text{Uptake}$ of $\text{Glucose}$ by $\text{Body}$ $\text{Cells}$ and the $\text{Storage}$ of $\text{Glucose}$ as $\text{Glycogen}$ in the $\text{Liver}$, thereby $\text{Lowering}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Sugar}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Substances}$ is $\text{Digested}$ in the $\text{Stomach}$?
explanation: $\text{Protein}$ $\text{Digestion}$ $\text{Begins}$ in the $\text{Stomach}$ with the $\text{Action}$ of $\text{Pepsin}$ ($	ext{Activated}$ by $\text{HCl}$). $\text{Starch}$ begins in the $\text{Mouth}$, and most $\text{Fat}$ $\text{Digestion}$ occurs in the $\text{Small}$ $\text{Intestine}$.

text: The $\text{Transmission}$ of $\text{Acquired}$ $\text{Immune}$ $\text{Deficiency}$ $\text{Syndrome}$ ($	ext{AIDS}$) is $\text{Possible}$ through:
explanation: $\text{AIDS}$ is caused by the $\text{Human}$ $\text{Immunodeficiency}$ $\text{Virus}$ ($	ext{HIV}$), which is $\text{Transmitted}$ primarily through $\text{Unprotected}$ $\text{Sexual}$ $\text{Contact}$, $\text{Contaminated}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Transfusions}$, and from $\text{Mother}$ to $\text{Child}$.

text: Which $\text{Term}$ describes the $\text{Role}$ played by an $\text{Organism}$ in its $\text{Environment}$?
explanation: The $\text{Niche}$ is the $\text{Functional}$ $\text{Role}$ or $\text{Position}$ of a $\text{Species}$ within an $\text{Ecosystem}$, including its $\text{Interactions}$ with $\text{Other}$ $\text{Organisms}$ and its $\text{Use}$ of $\text{Resources}$.

text: The $\text{Organ}$ in $\text{Mammals}$ where $\text{Fertilization}$ $\text{Usually}$ $\text{Occurs}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the female mammalian reproductive system highlighting the Fallopian tube]
explanation: $\text{Fertilization}$ (the $\text{Fusion}$ of $\text{Sperm}$ and $\text{Egg}$) $\text{Typically}$ $\text{Occurs}$ in the $\text{Upper}$ $\text{Third}$ of the $\text{Oviduct}$ (Fallopian $\text{Tube}$).

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Brain}$ that $\text{Controls}$ $\text{Balance}$ and $\text{Posture}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the human brain highlighting the Cerebellum]
explanation: The $\text{Cerebellum}$ is $\text{Located}$ at the $\text{Back}$ of the $\text{Brain}$ $\text{Beneath}$ the $\text{Cerebrum}$ and is $\text{Crucial}$ for $\text{Coordinating}$ $\text{Voluntary}$ $\text{Movements}$, $\text{Balance}$, and $\text{Posture}$.

text: Which of the following $\text{Processes}$ is $\text{Dependent}$ on the $\text{Force}$ of $\text{Gravity}$ for $\text{Transport}$?
explanation: $\text{Transpiration}$ $\text{Pull}$ creates a $\text{Tension}$ in the $\text{Xylem}$ that $\text{Pulls}$ the $\text{Water}$ $\text{Column}$ upwards, $\text{Working}$ $\text{Against}$ the $\text{Force}$ of $\text{Gravity}$.

text: The $\text{Adaptive}$ $\text{Coloration}$ that allows an $\text{Organism}$ to $\text{Blend}$ with its $\text{Environment}$ is known as:
image: [Image illustrating camouflage (e.g., a chameleon or stick insect)]
explanation: $\text{Camouflage}$ ($	ext{Cryptic}$ $\text{Coloration}$) is the use of $\text{Any}$ $\text{Combination}$ of $\text{Materials}$, $\text{Coloration}$, or $\text{Illumination}$ for $\text{Concealment}$ or $\text{Blending}$.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cell}$ that $\text{Regulates}$ the $\text{Passage}$ of $\text{Substances}$ in and out is the:
image: [Diagram of a plant cell highlighting the cell membrane]
explanation: The $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Membrane}$ ($	ext{Plasma}$ $\text{Membrane}$) is $\text{Selectively}$ $\text{Permeable}$, $\text{Controlling}$ what $\text{Substances}$ $\text{Enter}$ and $\text{Leave}$ the $\text{Cell}$.

text: The $\text{Function}$ of $\text{Stomata}$ in $\text{Plants}$ is primarily for:
image: [Microscopic image of an open stoma with guard cells]
explanation: $\text{Stomata}$ are $\text{Tiny}$ $\text{Pores}$ on the $\text{Epidermis}$ of $\text{Leaves}$ $\text{Controlled}$ by $\text{Guard}$ $\text{Cells}$. They $\text{Allow}$ $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ to $\text{Enter}$ and $\text{Oxygen}$ and $\text{Water}$ $\text{Vapour}$ to $\text{Leave}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Organisms}$ undergoes $\text{Incomplete}$ $\text{Metamorphosis}$?
image: [Life cycle diagrams comparing complete and incomplete metamorphosis]
explanation: $\text{Incomplete}$ $\text{Metamorphosis}$ ($	ext{Hemimetabolism}$) involves $\text{Three}$ $\text{Stages}$: $\text{Egg}$, $\text{Nymph}$, and $\text{Adult}$. The $\text{Nymph}$ resembles a $\text{Smaller}$, $\text{Wingless}$ $\text{Adult}$. $\text{Grasshoppers}$ and $\text{Locusts}$ are examples. The others listed undergo $\text{Complete}$ $\text{Metamorphosis}$ ($	ext{Holometabolism}$).

text: The $\text{Organism}$ that $\text{Feeds}$ $\text{Only}$ on $\text{Plants}$ is known as a:
explanation: A $\text{Herbivore}$ is an $\text{Animal}$ that is $\text{Anatomically}$ and $\text{Physiologically}$ $\text{Adapted}$ to $\text{Eating}$ $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Material}$, for $\text{Example}$, $\text{Grasshoppers}$ or $\text{Cows}$.

text: The $\text{Main}$ $\text{Reason}$ for $\text{Conserving}$ $\text{Natural}$ $\text{Resources}$ is to:
explanation: $\text{Conservation}$ aims to $\text{Protect}$ and $\text{Manage}$ $\text{Natural}$ $\text{Resources}$ to $\text{Ensure}$ their $\text{Long}$-$\text{Term}$ $\text{Availability}$ and $\text{Ecological}$ $\text{Balance}$ ($	ext{Sustainability}$).

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Uptake}$ of $\text{Water}$ by $\text{Dry}$ $\text{Seeds}$ during $\text{Germination}$ is called:
explanation: $\text{Imbibition}$ is the $\text{Absorption}$ of $\text{Water}$ by $\text{Solid}$ $\text{Particles}$ ($	ext{Colloids}$) of the $\text{Seed}$, $\text{Causing}$ them to $\text{Swell}$ and eventually $\text{Break}$ the $\text{Seed}$ $\text{Coat}$ to initiate $\text{Germination}$.

text: The $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Cross}$ between a $\text{Homozygous}$ $\text{Dominant}$ $\text{Individual}$ and a $\text{Homozygous}$ $\text{Recessive}$ $\text{Individual}$ yields $\text{Offspring}$ that are all:
image: [Punnett square for a monohybrid cross (AA x aa)]
explanation: A cross between $\text{AA}$ ($	ext{Homozygous}$ $\text{Dominant}$) and $\text{aa}$ ($	ext{Homozygous}$ $\text{Recessive}$) results in $\text{100\%}$ $\text{Aa}$ ($	ext{Heterozygous}$) $\text{Offspring}$ in the $\text{F1}$ $\text{Generation}$.

text: The $\text{Study}$ of $\text{Interactions}$ between $\text{Organisms}$ and their $\text{Environment}$ is known as:
explanation: $\text{Ecology}$ is the $\text{Scientific}$ $\text{Study}$ of the $\text{Distributions}$ and $\text{Abundance}$ of $\text{Living}$ $\text{Organisms}$ and how they are $\text{Affected}$ by $\text{Interactions}$ between $\text{Themselves}$ and their $\text{Environment}$.
